reuse.why: Factors the range rule into getRangeAmount and has getScheduledAmount use it, but the five server sites call the new range-only helper instead of the existing getScheduledAmount, which already handles missing, numeric and ranged amounts.

duplication.why: The midpoint copies are removed, but each site keeps its own `missing ? 0 : number ? value : range` dispatch, duplicating what getScheduledAmount already decides.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, and call sites import it from there.

scope.why: Only the ranged-amount computations, their comments and a test are touched.

maintainability.why: The worst-case rule has one definition, but having two helpers (range-only and full) and five hand-written dispatches invites the next rule change (e.g. approximate amounts) to be applied inconsistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, schedule-template.ts createScheduleList and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions use getRangeAmount inside their own type dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The per-site dispatches are pre-existing and left in place openly, not reshaped.

one_place.where: getRangeAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts is used by getScheduledAmount and by all five server-side sites; the surrounding missing/numeric dispatch remains per site.
